cards.back:
1. **Proton number**: the number of **protons** in the **nucleus** of an atom.
2. **Nucleon number**: the **total number of protons and neutrons** in the **nucleus** of an atom.

Trap: nucleon number is **not** the same as relative atomic mass.

Atoms of the **same element** with the **same number of protons** but **different numbers of neutrons**.

Trap: say **atoms**, not 'elements'. Isotopes have the **same chemical properties** (same electron configuration) but **different physical properties** (mass, density).

A **region of space** around the nucleus that can hold **up to two electrons**, with **opposite spins**.

Shapes: s = spherical, p = dumbbell.

cards.front:
Define **shell**, **sub-shell** and **principal quantum number, n**.

Define · 1.3.1
cards.back:
1. **Principal quantum number, n**: the number of the **main energy level** (shell) an electron is in, $n = 1, 2, 3 \dots$
2. **Shell**: a group of orbitals with the **same principal quantum number**.
3. **Sub-shell**: a group of orbitals of the **same type** (s, p or d) within a shell (s = 1 orbital, p = 3, d = 5).
The electronic configuration of an atom or ion with its electrons in the **lowest available energy levels** (the **lowest energy** arrangement).

The energy required to **remove one electron** from **each atom** in **one mole** of **gaseous atoms** to form **one mole of gaseous 1+ ions**.
$$\ce{Na(g) -> Na+(g) + e-}$$
Trap: lose the mark if you leave out **gaseous**, **one mole** or the **state symbols** in the equation.

cards.front:
Define **second ionisation energy** (successive ionisation energies).

Define · 1.4.1
cards.back:
The energy required to **remove one electron** from **each ion** in **one mole** of **gaseous 1+ ions** to form **one mole of gaseous 2+ ions**.
$$\ce{Na+(g) -> Na^2+(g) + e-}$$
In general, the $n$th IE starts from gaseous $(n-1)$+ ions and forms gaseous $n$+ ions.

Trap: it is **not** the energy to remove two electrons from the atom.

cards.front:
Define the **unified atomic mass unit**.

Define · 2.1.1
cards.back:
**One twelfth** of the **mass of a carbon-12 atom**.

(Symbol u; $1\,\text{u} \approx 1.66 \times 10^{-27}$ kg.)

The **weighted mean (average) mass** of an **atom** of an element compared with **one twelfth** of the **mass of an atom of carbon-12**.

Trap: **weighted** mean, because it takes account of the abundance of each isotope.

The **mass of an atom of an isotope** compared with **one twelfth** of the **mass of an atom of carbon-12**.

Trap: no 'weighted mean' here, it is one isotope.
The **weighted mean (average) mass** of a **molecule** compared with **one twelfth** of the **mass of an atom of carbon-12**.

The **weighted mean (average) mass** of one **formula unit** of a compound compared with **one twelfth** of the **mass of an atom of carbon-12**.

Used for **ionic compounds** (e.g. NaCl), which do not have molecules.

cards.front:
Define the **mole** (in terms of the Avogadro constant).

Define · 2.2.1
cards.back:
1. **Mole**: the **amount of substance** that contains the **Avogadro constant** number of particles (atoms, molecules, ions or electrons), $6.02 \times 10^{23}$.
2. **Avogadro constant, L**: the number of particles in **one mole**, $6.02 \times 10^{23}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$.

Memory hook: 1 mol = 'chemist's dozen' of $6.02 \times 10^{23}$.

1. **Empirical formula**: the **simplest whole-number ratio** of the **atoms of each element** in a compound.
2. **Molecular formula**: the **actual number of atoms** of each element in **one molecule** of a compound.

Example: ethane is $\ce{C2H6}$ (molecular), $\ce{CH3}$ (empirical).

1. **Water of crystallisation**: water molecules that are **chemically bonded** into the **crystal lattice** of a salt in a **fixed ratio**.
2. **Hydrated**: a substance that **contains water of crystallisation** (e.g. $\ce{CuSO4.5H2O}$).
3. **Anhydrous**: a substance that **contains no water** (of crystallisation) (e.g. $\ce{CuSO4}$).

The **power of an atom** to **attract electrons to itself** (syllabus wording).

Mark schemes also accept: '…to attract the **bonding pair of electrons** in a **covalent bond**'.
Increases **across a period** and **up a group** (F is the most electronegative).
The **electrostatic attraction** between **oppositely charged ions**.

The **electrostatic attraction** between **positive metal ions** and **delocalised electrons**.

Trap: say **positive ions**, not 'nuclei' or 'atoms'.
The **electrostatic attraction** between the **nuclei of two atoms** and a **shared pair of electrons**.

A **covalent bond** in which **both electrons** in the shared pair are **provided by the same atom**.

Example: $\ce{NH3 + H+ -> NH4+}$ (N donates its **lone pair** to $\ce{H+}$).
Shown with an arrow from donor to acceptor.

1. **σ bond**: formed by the **direct (end-on / head-on) overlap** of orbitals **between the bonding atoms**.
2. **π bond**: formed by the **sideways overlap** of adjacent **p orbitals**, giving electron density **above and below** the plane of the σ bond.

Single bond = 1σ. Double bond = 1σ + 1π. Triple bond = 1σ + 2π.
Trap: π bonds are **weaker** than σ bonds (less overlap).

cards.front:
What is meant by **hybridisation** (sp, sp², sp³)?

Define · 3.4.2
cards.back:
The **mixing** of atomic orbitals (s and p) on an atom to form **new hybrid orbitals** of **equal energy**.

1. **sp³**: 4 orbitals, **109.5°** (e.g. $\ce{CH4}$).
2. **sp²**: 3 orbitals, **120°**, 1 unhybridised p left for a π bond (e.g. $\ce{C2H4}$).
3. **sp**: 2 orbitals, **180°**, 2 p left for 2 π bonds (e.g. $\ce{C2H2}$).

1. **Bond energy**: the energy **required to break one mole** of a **particular covalent bond** in the **gaseous state**.
2. **Bond length**: the **internuclear distance** between **two covalently bonded atoms**.

Trap: bond breaking is always **endothermic** (bond energy is positive). Some are **exact** (e.g. H–H), others are **average** values from many compounds (e.g. C–H).

The attraction between a **lone pair** on a **highly electronegative atom** (**N, O** or F) and a **δ+ hydrogen atom** that is **covalently bonded to N, O or F** on another molecule.

In a diagram show: **δ+ / δ− dipoles**, the **lone pair**, and the H bond as a **dashed line** in a **straight line** (about 180°) with the O–H / N–H bond.
It is a special, strong type of **pd–pd** attraction.

The **generic term** for **all intermolecular forces** (forces between molecules).

Includes:
1. **id–id** (instantaneous dipole–induced dipole, London dispersion) forces: in **all** molecules; stronger with **more electrons**.
2. **pd–pd** (permanent dipole–permanent dipole) forces: between **polar** molecules.
(Hydrogen bonding is a special, stronger case of pd–pd.)

Trap: these are **between** molecules, not the covalent bonds **within** them.

1. Temperature **298 K** (25 °C).
2. Pressure **101 kPa** (1 atm).
3. Solutions at **1 mol dm⁻³**.
4. All substances in their **standard states** (normal physical state under these conditions).

Shown by the symbol ⦵, e.g. $\Delta H^\ominus$.

1. **Exothermic**: **heat energy is released** to the surroundings; $\Delta H$ is **negative**.
2. **Endothermic**: **heat energy is absorbed** from the surroundings; $\Delta H$ is **positive**.

(Enthalpy change, $\Delta H$ = heat energy change at **constant pressure**.)

cards.front:
Define **standard enthalpy change of reaction, $\Delta H_r$**.

Define · 5.1.3
cards.back: The **enthalpy change** when the **amounts of reactants shown in the equation** react to give products, under **standard conditions**, with all substances in their **standard states**.

cards.front:
Define **standard enthalpy change of formation, $\Delta H_f$**.

Define · 5.1.3
cards.back:
The **enthalpy change** when **one mole** of a **compound** is **formed from its elements** in their **standard states**, under **standard conditions**.
$$\ce{C(s) + 2H2(g) -> CH4(g)}$$
Trap: $\Delta H_f$ of an **element** in its standard state is **zero**. Use **½ O₂** etc. so only 1 mol of product forms.

cards.front:
Define **standard enthalpy change of combustion, $\Delta H_c$**.

Define · 5.1.3
cards.back:
The **enthalpy change** when **one mole** of a substance is **burned completely** in **excess oxygen**, under **standard conditions**.
$$\ce{CH4(g) + 2O2(g) -> CO2(g) + 2H2O(l)}$$
Trap: water is **liquid** under standard conditions. Always **exothermic**.

cards.front:
Define **standard enthalpy change of neutralisation, $\Delta H_{neut}$**.

Define · 5.1.3
cards.back:
The **enthalpy change** when **one mole of water** is **formed** by the reaction of an **acid** with an **alkali** (base), under **standard conditions**.
$$\ce{H+(aq) + OH-(aq) -> H2O(l)}$$
Trap: **per mole of water**, not per mole of acid ($\ce{H2SO4}$ gives 2 mol water). Weak acids give a **less exothermic** value (energy used to dissociate).

The **total enthalpy change** for a reaction is **independent of the route** taken, provided the **initial and final conditions are the same**.

Used to build energy cycles for enthalpy changes that **can't be measured directly**.

1. **Oxidation**: **loss of electrons** / **increase in oxidation number**.
2. **Reduction**: **gain of electrons** / **decrease in oxidation number**.
3. **Redox**: a reaction in which **oxidation and reduction occur at the same time**.

Memory hook: **OIL RIG** (Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain).

A redox reaction in which the **same element** is **simultaneously oxidised and reduced**.
$$\ce{Cl2 + 2NaOH -> NaCl + NaClO + H2O}$$
Cl: **0 → −1** (reduced) and **0 → +1** (oxidised).
Trap: always show the **oxidation numbers** to earn the mark.

1. **Oxidising agent**: a species that **oxidises** another species by **accepting electrons**; it is **itself reduced**.
2. **Reducing agent**: a species that **reduces** another species by **donating electrons**; it is **itself oxidised**.
A reaction in which the **products can react to re-form the reactants**: it can go in **both directions** ($\rightleftharpoons$).

1. The **rate of the forward reaction** is **equal** to the **rate of the reverse reaction**.
2. The **concentrations** of reactants and products **remain constant**.
3. Only in a **closed system**.

Trap: concentrations are **constant**, **not equal**. Both reactions are still **happening** (that's why it's 'dynamic').

If a **change is made** to a system at **dynamic equilibrium**, the **position of equilibrium moves** to **minimise (oppose) this change**.

Trap: only a **temperature** change alters the value of $K_c$ / $K_p$. A **catalyst** does **not** move the position, it only helps equilibrium be reached faster.

1. **Mole fraction** of a gas = $\dfrac{\text{moles of that gas}}{\text{total moles of gas}}$
2. **Partial pressure** = the pressure a gas in a mixture would exert if it **alone occupied the container**:
$$p_A = \text{mole fraction of A} \times p_{total}$$
The partial pressures add up to the total pressure.

1. **Acid**: a **proton ($\ce{H+}$) donor**.
2. **Base**: a **proton ($\ce{H+}$) acceptor**.

cards.front:
Define **strong acid / strong base** and **weak acid / weak base**.

Define · 7.2.4
cards.back:
1. **Strong** acid/base: **fully (completely) dissociated** in **aqueous solution**.
2. **Weak** acid/base: **partially dissociated** in **aqueous solution**.
$$\ce{HCl -> H+ + Cl-}\qquad\ce{CH3COOH <=> H+ + CH3COO-}$$
Trap: **strong ≠ concentrated**. Strength is about **degree of dissociation**, concentration is about **amount per dm³**.

The **change in concentration** of a **reactant or product** per **unit time**.

Units: $\text{mol dm}^{-3}\ \text{s}^{-1}$.

cards.front:
What is meant by **effective** and **non-effective collisions**?

Define · 8.1.1
cards.back:
1. **Effective collision**: a collision between particles with **energy ≥ activation energy** (and the **correct orientation**) that **leads to a reaction**.
2. **Non-effective collision**: a collision that does **not** lead to a reaction (energy **< $E_A$** or wrong orientation); particles just bounce apart.

The **minimum energy** required for a **collision to be effective** (syllabus wording).

i.e. the minimum energy colliding particles need for a reaction to happen.

1. **Catalyst**: a substance that **increases the rate of a reaction** but is **chemically unchanged at the end**.
2. It provides an **alternative pathway** (**different mechanism**) with a **lower activation energy**.
3. **Catalysis**: the **increase in rate** of a reaction caused by a catalyst.

Explain with the **Boltzmann distribution**: lower $E_A$ means **more particles** have energy **≥ $E_A$**, so **more effective collisions per unit time**.

cards.front:
What does the **Boltzmann distribution** show?

Define · 8.3
cards.back:
The **distribution of molecular energies** (number of molecules with each energy) in a sample of **gas** at a **given temperature**.

1. Curve starts at the **origin** (no molecules with zero energy).
2. **Never touches** the energy axis at high energy.
3. **Area under curve** = total number of molecules.
4. Higher T: peak moves **right and lower**, **same area**, more molecules beyond $E_A$.

cards.topic: An introduction to AS Level organic chemistry
cards.back:
A **compound** made up of **carbon and hydrogen atoms only**.

Trap: 'only' is the mark.

cards.topic: An introduction to AS Level organic chemistry
cards.back:
A family of compounds with:
1. the **same functional group**,
2. the **same general formula**,
3. each member differing by **$\ce{CH2}$**,
4. **similar chemical properties**,
5. a **gradual trend** in **physical properties** (e.g. boiling point).

cards.topic: An introduction to AS Level organic chemistry
cards.back:
An **atom or group of atoms** in a molecule that is **responsible for the characteristic chemical reactions** of that compound.

Examples: $\ce{-OH}$, $\ce{C=C}$, $\ce{-COOH}$.

cards.topic: An introduction to AS Level organic chemistry
cards.back:
1. **Saturated**: contains **only single C–C bonds** (no multiple bonds).
2. **Unsaturated**: contains **one or more C=C double (or C≡C triple) bonds**.

Test: unsaturated compounds **decolourise bromine water** (orange → colourless).

cards.topic: An introduction to AS Level organic chemistry
cards.back:
1. **Homolytic fission**: a covalent bond breaks so that **each atom takes one electron** from the bonding pair, forming **two free radicals**.
2. **Heterolytic fission**: a covalent bond breaks so that **one atom takes both electrons**, forming a **cation and an anion**.

Curly arrows: **half** (fish-hook) arrows for homolytic, **full** arrows for heterolytic.

cards.topic: An introduction to AS Level organic chemistry
cards.back:
A species with **one or more unpaired electrons**.

Shown with a dot, e.g. $\ce{Cl^.}$, $\ce{CH3^.}$. Very **reactive**.

cards.topic: An introduction to AS Level organic chemistry
cards.back:
1. **Initiation**: **free radicals are formed** by **homolytic fission** (UV light): $\ce{Cl2 -> 2Cl^.}$
2. **Propagation**: a **free radical reacts with a molecule** to form a product **and a new free radical**:
$\ce{CH4 + Cl^. -> CH3^. + HCl}$
$\ce{CH3^. + Cl2 -> CH3Cl + Cl^.}$
3. **Termination**: **two free radicals combine** to form a **molecule**: $\ce{CH3^. + Cl^. -> CH3Cl}$

cards.topic: An introduction to AS Level organic chemistry
cards.back:
1. **Nucleophile**: a species that **donates a lone pair of electrons** (**electron-pair donor**) to form a new covalent bond; attacks a **δ+ carbon** (e.g. $\ce{OH-}$, $\ce{CN-}$, $\ce{NH3}$).
2. **Electrophile**: a species that **accepts a pair of electrons** (**electron-pair acceptor**); attracted to an **electron-rich** region such as a C=C (e.g. $\ce{Br2}$, $\ce{H+}$, $\ce{NO2+}$).

cards.topic: An introduction to AS Level organic chemistry
cards.back:
1. **Addition**: **two molecules join** to form **one product** (e.g. across a C=C).
2. **Substitution**: **one atom or group** is **replaced** by **another** atom or group.
3. **Elimination**: a **small molecule** (e.g. $\ce{H2O}$ or HX) is **removed** from a larger molecule, forming a **C=C** double bond.

cards.topic: An introduction to AS Level organic chemistry
cards.back:
1. **Hydrolysis**: the **breaking of a bond** by **reaction with water** (often with acid or $\ce{OH-}$ to speed it up).
2. **Condensation**: **two molecules join together** with the **loss of a small molecule** such as **water** (or HCl).

cards.topic: An introduction to AS Level organic chemistry
cards.front:
Define **oxidation** and **reduction** in organic chemistry.

Define · 13.2
cards.back:
1. **Oxidation**: **addition of oxygen** or **removal of hydrogen** (shown as [O]).
2. **Reduction**: **addition of hydrogen** or **removal of oxygen** (shown as [H]).

cards.topic: An introduction to AS Level organic chemistry
cards.front:
Define **structural isomers** and the three types.

Define · 13.4
cards.back:
**Structural isomers**: compounds with the **same molecular formula** but **different structural formulae**.
1. **Chain**: different **carbon skeleton** (straight vs branched).
2. **Positional**: functional group in a **different position** on the same chain.
3. **Functional group**: **different functional groups** (e.g. alcohol vs ether, aldehyde vs ketone).

cards.topic: An introduction to AS Level organic chemistry
cards.back:
Compounds with the **same molecular formula** and the **same structural formula** but a **different arrangement of atoms in space**.

Two types: **geometrical (cis/trans)** and **optical**.

cards.topic: An introduction to AS Level organic chemistry
cards.front:
What is meant by **geometrical (cis/trans) isomerism**?

Define · 13.4
cards.back:
Stereoisomerism caused by **restricted rotation about a C=C double bond** (the π bond), where **each carbon of the C=C** has **two different atoms or groups** attached.

1. **cis**: same groups on the **same side**.
2. **trans**: same groups on **opposite sides**.
Trap: but-1-ene has **no** cis/trans isomers (one C has two H's).

cards.topic: An introduction to AS Level organic chemistry
cards.back:
1. **Chiral centre**: a **carbon atom** with **four different atoms or groups** attached.
2. **Optical isomers** (enantiomers): **non-superimposable mirror images** of each other.

Trap: draw them **3D** (wedge and dash) as **mirror images** to get the mark.

In **electrophilic addition** of HX to an **unsymmetrical alkene**, the **H atom adds to the carbon that already has more H atoms**, so X goes on the more substituted carbon.

Why: the **major product** comes from the **more stable carbocation**. Stability: **tertiary > secondary > primary**, because **alkyl groups** are **electron-donating** (**positive inductive effect**) and spread out the positive charge.
Example: propene + HBr → mainly **2-bromopropane**.

cards.front:
Define **standard enthalpy change of atomisation, $\Delta H_{at}$**.

Define · A Level 23.1.1
cards.back:
The **enthalpy change** when **one mole of gaseous atoms** is **formed from the element** in its **standard state**, under **standard conditions**.
$$\tfrac{1}{2}\ce{Cl2(g) -> Cl(g)}$$
Always **endothermic**.
Trap: per mole of **atoms formed**, so for $\ce{Cl2}$ it is **½ the bond energy**.

cards.front:
Define **lattice energy, $\Delta H_{latt}$**.

Define · A Level 23.1.1
cards.back:
The **enthalpy change** when **one mole** of an **ionic compound** is **formed from its gaseous ions** under **standard conditions**.
$$\ce{Na+(g) + Cl-(g) -> NaCl(s)}$$
Always **exothermic** (negative).
More exothermic with **smaller ions** and **higher charges**.
Trap: Cambridge defines it as **formation** from gaseous ions, not breaking up the lattice.

cards.front:
Define **first electron affinity**.

Define · A Level 23.1.2
cards.back:
The **enthalpy change** when **one electron is added** to **each atom** in **one mole of gaseous atoms** to form **one mole of gaseous 1− ions**.
$$\ce{Cl(g) + e- -> Cl-(g)}$$
Usually **exothermic**.

cards.front:
Define **second electron affinity**.

Define · A Level 23.1.2
cards.back:
The **enthalpy change** when **one electron is added** to **each ion** in **one mole of gaseous 1− ions** to form **one mole of gaseous 2− ions**.
$$\ce{O-(g) + e- -> O^2-(g)}$$
Always **endothermic**: the electron is added to a **negative ion**, so energy is needed to overcome the **repulsion**.

cards.front:
Define **standard enthalpy change of hydration, $\Delta H_{hyd}$**.

Define · A Level 23.2.1
cards.back:
The **enthalpy change** when **one mole** of **gaseous ions** **dissolves in sufficient water** to form an **infinitely dilute solution**, under **standard conditions**.
$$\ce{Na+(g) -> Na+(aq)}$$
Always **exothermic**. More exothermic for **smaller ions** with **higher charge** (higher charge density).

cards.front:
Define **standard enthalpy change of solution, $\Delta H_{sol}$**.

Define · A Level 23.2.1
cards.back:
The **enthalpy change** when **one mole** of an **ionic solid** **dissolves in sufficient water** to form an **infinitely dilute solution**, under **standard conditions**.
$$\ce{NaCl(s) -> Na+(aq) + Cl-(aq)}$$
Can be **exothermic or endothermic**.
$$\Delta H_{sol} = \Sigma\Delta H_{hyd} - \Delta H_{latt}$$

The **number of possible arrangements** of the **particles and their energy** in a **given system** (syllabus wording).

i.e. a measure of **disorder**. Entropy increases: **solid → liquid → gas**, more **moles of gas**, higher **temperature**, **dissolving**.
Units: $\text{J K}^{-1}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$ (note **J**, not kJ).

cards.front:
State the **Gibbs equation** and when a reaction is **feasible**.

Define · A Level 23.4.1
cards.back:
$$\Delta G^\ominus = \Delta H^\ominus - T\Delta S^\ominus$$
1. A reaction is **feasible** (spontaneous) when $\Delta G^\ominus$ is **negative** ($\le 0$).
2. $T$ in **kelvin**; convert $\Delta S$ from J to **kJ** (÷ 1000).

Trap: feasible does **not** mean fast. A high **activation energy** can make a feasible reaction too slow to see (**kinetics**).

cards.front:
Define the **Faraday constant, F**, and state its link to L.

Define · A Level 24.1.2
cards.back:
The **charge carried by one mole of electrons**: $F \approx 96\,500\ \text{C mol}^{-1}$.
$$F = L \times e$$
$L$ = Avogadro constant, $e$ = charge on one electron ($1.60 \times 10^{-19}$ C).

cards.front:
Define **standard electrode (reduction) potential, $E^\ominus$**.

Define · A Level 24.2.1
cards.back:
The **potential difference (EMF)** of a **half-cell** compared with (connected to) a **standard hydrogen electrode**, under **standard conditions**:
1. **298 K**
2. **101 kPa** (for gases)
3. **1.00 mol dm⁻³** solutions of ions.

Written as a **reduction**, e.g. $\ce{Cu^2+ + 2e- <=> Cu}$, $E^\ominus = +0.34$ V.

cards.front:
Define **standard cell potential, $E^\ominus_{cell}$**.

Define · A Level 24.2.1
cards.back:
The **potential difference (EMF)** between **two half-cells** connected together, under **standard conditions** (298 K, 101 kPa, 1.00 mol dm⁻³).
$$E^\ominus_{cell} = E^\ominus_{\text{positive}} - E^\ominus_{\text{negative}}$$
A reaction is **feasible** if $E^\ominus_{cell}$ is **positive**.

cards.front:
Define **conjugate acid** and **conjugate base**.

Define · A Level 25.1.1
cards.back:
A **conjugate acid–base pair** is two species that **differ by one proton ($\ce{H+}$)**.
1. **Conjugate base**: what is left when an **acid donates a proton**.
2. **Conjugate acid**: what forms when a **base accepts a proton**.
$$\ce{CH3COOH + H2O <=> CH3COO- + H3O+}$$
$\ce{CH3COOH}$/$\ce{CH3COO-}$ and $\ce{H3O+}$/$\ce{H2O}$ are the pairs.

$$\text{pH} = -\log_{10}[\ce{H+}]$$
Trap: $[\ce{H+}]$ in **mol dm⁻³**. pH has **no units**.

For $\ce{HA <=> H+ + A-}$:
$$K_a = \frac{[\ce{H+}][\ce{A-}]}{[\ce{HA}]}$$
$$\text{p}K_a = -\log_{10} K_a$$
Larger $K_a$ (smaller $\text{p}K_a$) = **stronger** weak acid.
Units of $K_a$: $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$.

cards.front:
Define **$K_w$** (ionic product of water).

Define · A Level 25.1.3
cards.back:
$$K_w = [\ce{H+}][\ce{OH-}]$$
$= 1.00 \times 10^{-14}\ \text{mol}^2\ \text{dm}^{-6}$ at **298 K**.

Trap: the value **changes with temperature**. Pure water is always **neutral** ($[\ce{H+}] = [\ce{OH-}]$) even when its pH isn't 7.

cards.front:
Define a **buffer solution**.

Define · A Level 25.1.5
cards.back:
A solution that **resists changes in pH** (pH stays almost constant) when **small amounts of acid or alkali** are added.

Made from a **weak acid and its conjugate base** (e.g. $\ce{CH3COOH}$ / $\ce{CH3COONa}$), or a weak base and its conjugate acid.
Trap: 'resists change', **not** 'pH doesn't change at all'.

The **product of the concentrations of the ions** in a **saturated solution** of a **sparingly soluble salt**, each raised to the **power of its coefficient** in the equation, at a given temperature.
$$\ce{PbCl2(s) <=> Pb^2+(aq) + 2Cl-(aq)}$$
$$K_{sp} = [\ce{Pb^2+}][\ce{Cl-}]^2$$
Trap: the **solid is not** in the expression. Work out units each time.

cards.front:
What is the **common ion effect**?

Define · A Level 25.1
cards.back:
The **reduction in the solubility** of a sparingly soluble salt when it is in a solution that **already contains one of its ions**.

Why: the added ion pushes the equilibrium $\ce{AgCl(s) <=> Ag+(aq) + Cl-(aq)}$ to the **left**, so **more solid precipitates** ($K_{sp}$ stays the same).

cards.front:
State what is meant by **partition coefficient, $K_{pc}$**.

Define · A Level 25.2.1
cards.back:
The **ratio of the concentrations** of a **solute** in **two immiscible solvents** when the system is at **equilibrium** (at a given temperature).
$$K_{pc} = \frac{[\text{X}]_{\text{solvent 1}}}{[\text{X}]_{\text{solvent 2}}}$$
Trap: say which solvent is on **top** of the fraction.

cards.front:
Define **rate equation**, **rate constant** and **order of reaction**.

Define · A Level 26.1.1
cards.back:
1. **Rate equation**: $\text{rate} = k[\text{A}]^m[\text{B}]^n$, found by **experiment** (not from the balanced equation).
2. **Rate constant, k**: the **proportionality constant** in the rate equation.
3. **Order with respect to a reactant**: the **power** to which its **concentration** is raised in the rate equation ($m$ or $n$).
4. **Overall order**: the **sum of the orders** ($m + n$).

Trap: $k$ changes with **temperature** only (and a catalyst), not with concentration.

The **time taken** for the **concentration of a reactant** to **fall to half** of its **original (initial) value**.

For a **first-order** reaction, half-life is **constant**:
$$k = \frac{0.693}{t_{1/2}}$$

cards.front:
Define **rate-determining step** and **intermediate**.

Define · A Level 26.1.1
cards.back:
1. **Rate-determining step**: the **slowest step** in a reaction mechanism. Species in the rate equation appear in (or before) this step.
2. **Intermediate**: a species **formed in one step** of the mechanism and **used up in a later step**, so it does **not** appear in the overall equation.

Trap: an intermediate is **not** the same as a transition state, and not a catalyst (a catalyst is used up first, then **regenerated**).

cards.front:
Define **homogeneous** and **heterogeneous catalyst**.

Define · A Level 26.3
cards.back:
1. **Homogeneous**: catalyst in the **same phase** as the reactants (e.g. $\ce{Fe^2+}$/$\ce{Fe^3+}$ in $\ce{I-}$ + $\ce{S2O8^2-}$).
2. **Heterogeneous**: catalyst in a **different phase** from the reactants (e.g. **Fe** in the Haber process; **Pt/Rh/Pd** in catalytic converters).

Heterogeneous mechanism: **adsorption** → bonds weaken / react → **desorption**.

A **d-block element** which forms **one or more stable ions** with **incomplete d orbitals** (syllabus wording).

Trap: **Sc** and **Zn** are d-block but **not** transition elements ($\ce{Sc^3+}$ is $3d^0$, $\ce{Zn^2+}$ is $3d^{10}$).

A **species** that contains a **lone pair of electrons** that forms a **dative covalent bond** to a **central metal atom/ion**.

Examples: $\ce{H2O}$, $\ce{NH3}$, $\ce{Cl-}$, $\ce{CN-}$.

A **molecule or ion** formed by a **central metal atom/ion** **surrounded by one or more ligands**.

Example: $\ce{[Cu(H2O)6]^2+}$.

The **number of dative (coordinate) bonds** formed between the **ligands** and the **central metal ion**.

Example: $\ce{[Cu(H2O)6]^2+}$ = 6, $\ce{[CuCl4]^2-}$ = 4.
Trap: it is **bonds**, not ligands. 3 bidentate en ligands → coordination number **6**.

cards.front:
Define **monodentate**, **bidentate** and **polydentate** ligands.

Define · A Level 28.2.3
cards.back:
1. **Monodentate**: forms **one** dative bond to the central metal ion (e.g. $\ce{H2O}$, $\ce{NH3}$, $\ce{Cl-}$).
2. **Bidentate**: forms **two** dative bonds (e.g. **ethane-1,2-diamine** (en), **ethanedioate**).
3. **Polydentate** (multidentate): forms **more than two** dative bonds (e.g. **EDTA⁴⁻**, 6 bonds).

cards.front:
Define **degenerate** and **non-degenerate d orbitals**.

Define · A Level 28.3.1
cards.back:
1. **Degenerate**: d orbitals with the **same energy** (all five in an **isolated** metal ion).
2. **Non-degenerate**: d orbitals at **different energies**; the d orbitals **split** into two sets when **ligands** bond to the ion.

Octahedral: 3 lower, 2 higher. Tetrahedral: 2 lower, 3 higher.

The **equilibrium constant** for the **formation of the complex ion** in a **solvent** from its **constituent ions or molecules** (syllabus wording).
$$\ce{Cu^2+ + 4Cl- <=> [CuCl4]^2-}$$
$$K_{stab} = \frac{[\ce{[CuCl4]^2-}]}{[\ce{Cu^2+}][\ce{Cl-}]^4}$$
Trap: **water is left out** of the expression. Larger $K_{stab}$ = **more stable** complex.

cards.topic: An introduction to A Level organic chemistry
cards.front:
Define **optically active** and **racemic mixture**.

Define · A Level 29.4.2
cards.back:
1. **Optically active**: a substance that **rotates the plane of plane-polarised light**.
2. **Racemic mixture**: an **equimolar (50:50) mixture** of the **two optical isomers** (enantiomers); it is **optically inactive** because the rotations **cancel out**.

cards.front:
Define **$R_f$ value** (thin-layer chromatography).

Define · A Level 37.1.1
cards.back:
$$R_f = \frac{\text{distance moved by the spot}}{\text{distance moved by the solvent front}}$$
Both measured from the **baseline**. Value is always **less than 1**, no units.

cards.front:
Define **retention time** (gas chromatography).

Define · A Level 37.2.1
cards.back: The **time taken** for a component to travel from **injection** of the sample to **detection** (the **peak**).
